sections.name: Slack
sections.blurb: Built into every Slack workspace. Type / in the message box, or click the slash icon next to it.
sections.note: A few built-in commands (like /archive, /rename, /remove) can be limited to owners and admins.

commands.reason: Slack's list says /remind is for yourself; its reminder page only shows the channel format /remind [#channel] [what] [when]. Nothing official covers reminding another person, and the 'me' syntax isn't shown.
commands.does: Sets a reminder for yourself, or posts a reminder in a channel at the time you pick.
commands.add: For a channel: #channel, what, and when.

commands.reason: Real and current, but it only flips your availability to away or active. It does not set a custom status message.
commands.does: Switches you between away and active.

commands.reason: Real, but the official list shows no duration option, so the 'for 1 hour' example is unverified.
commands.does: Turns Do Not Disturb on or off to pause notifications.

commands.reason: Listed as 'Start a huddle'.
commands.does: Starts a huddle (a quick audio call) in the current conversation.

commands.reason: Listed for both DMs and channels: /msg [@someone] or [#channel] [your message].
commands.does: Sends a message to a person or a channel without leaving where you are.
commands.example: /msg @dana the deck is in the shared folder

commands.reason: Listed as /invite [@someone] [#channel].
commands.does: Adds someone to a channel.

commands.reason: Listed.
commands.does: Leaves the current channel.

commands.reason: Listed as 'Set the current channel topic'.
commands.does: Sets the topic shown at the top of the channel.
commands.example: /topic Launch week: questions here, decisions in the doc

commands.reason: Listed as /mute [#channel].
commands.does: Mutes or unmutes a conversation.
commands.add: Optional: #channel. Leave it off for the current one.

commands.reason: Listed as /search [your search terms].
commands.does: Searches messages and files.

commands.reason: Listed: appends the shrug to the end of your message.
commands.does: Adds ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ to the end of your message.
commands.example: /shrug no idea who moved the meeting

sections.name: Notion
sections.where: any Notion page (type / on a new line or in a block)
sections.blurb: Type / on a Notion page and keep typing to pick a block.
sections.note: Press Esc to close the / menu if you just want to type a slash.

commands.reason: Listed: creates a to-do list with checkboxes.
commands.does: Adds a checkbox to-do list.
commands.add: Your first task after it appears.

commands.reason: Listed: creates a toggle list.
commands.does: Adds a toggle list that opens and closes.
commands.add: A short title; tuck details inside.

commands.reason: Notion's styling page says 'Type /callout in your page and press enter.'
commands.does: Adds a highlighted box with an icon, for notes and warnings.
commands.add: The text you want to stand out.

commands.reason: Notion's page says to use the command /table for a simple table.
commands.does: Adds a simple table.
commands.add: Fill in rows and columns after it appears.

commands.reason: Listed: creates a code block.
commands.does: Adds a code block with syntax colors.
commands.add: Paste your code, then pick the language.

commands.reason: Listed: creates a quote block of larger text.
commands.does: Adds a larger quote block.

commands.reason: Listed, with /h2 and /h3 for smaller headings.
commands.does: Adds a large heading. /h2 and /h3 make smaller ones.

commands.reason: Listed: creates a light gray divider.
commands.does: Adds a light gray divider line.

commands.reason: Listed: creates a Table of Contents block.
commands.does: Adds a table of contents built from your headings.
commands.add: Nothing else needed; it updates itself.

commands.reason: Not a slash command in Notion's docs. Comments are added with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M, the Comment button on selected text, or the block menu.

sections.name: Discord
sections.where: the message box in a Discord text channel or DM
sections.blurb: Discord's own built-in commands, before any bots are added.
sections.note: Built-ins like /giphy, /nick and /me work even where a server turns off bot slash commands. /nick needs the server to allow nickname changes, and /tts only plays for people who have text-to-speech turned on.

commands.reason: Named as a built-in command in Discord's Slash Commands FAQ. Use this, not /gif, which has no official listing.
commands.does: Searches Giphy for a GIF to send.
commands.add: A word or two to search for.

commands.reason: Only confirmed in a 2021 Discord staff changelog ('giphy/tenor commands'), not in a current help page. Keep, but re-check it shows when you type /.
commands.does: Searches Tenor for a GIF to send.
commands.add: A word or two to search for.

commands.reason: Discord's Spoiler Tags page: 'typing /spoiler before your message.'
commands.does: Sends your message hidden until someone clicks it.

commands.reason: Named as a built-in in the Slash Commands FAQ.
commands.does: Changes your nickname in this server.

commands.reason: Named as a built-in in the Slash Commands FAQ.
commands.does: Sends your message styled as an action.

commands.reason: Real (Text-to-Speech 101), but listeners only hear it if they have text-to-speech notifications on, and the sender's server may block it.
commands.does: Sends your message to be read aloud to people in the channel who have text-to-speech on.

commands.reason: Discord's Threads FAQ only shows creating threads from the message menu or the Threads button. No official page lists a /thread command.
Confirmed as a desktop built-in in Discord's own developer changelog (2021). No current help page lists it.
commands.does: Adds (╯°□°)╯︵ ┻━┻ to your message.

commands.reason: Confirmed as a desktop built-in in Discord's own developer changelog (2021). No current help page lists it.
commands.does: Adds ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ to your message.

sections.name: Obsidian
sections.where: the Obsidian editor, at the start of a line or after a space
sections.prereq: Turn on Slash commands in Settings → Core plugins. Templates and Daily notes are separate core plugins you may also need to turn on.
sections.blurb: Typing / opens a search of Obsidian's commands. Type a few letters and press Enter. These aren't fixed commands; they're the words that find each one.
sections.note: Obsidian matches loosely, like its Command palette, so a few letters find any command. Press Esc or Space to close the search.

commands.reason: The command is 'Insert Table' (help page). /table is just search words that find it; say so.
commands.does: Finds Insert Table, which adds a Markdown table.
commands.add: Fill in the cells after it appears.

commands.reason: The command is 'Insert callout'; it adds a [!note] callout and can wrap selected text. /callout is search words.
commands.does: Finds Insert callout, which adds a note callout or wraps your selected text in one.
commands.add: Your note. Change the type, like [!tip], if you like.

commands.reason: Obsidian's help has no 'Insert code block' command (checked the official help source).
'Templates: Insert template' is documented. Needs the Templates core plugin and a templates folder.
commands.does: Finds Templates: Insert template. Needs the Templates core plugin.
commands.add: Pick a template from your templates folder.

commands.reason: 'Templates: Insert current date' is documented. Needs the Templates core plugin.
commands.does: Finds Templates: Insert current date. Needs the Templates core plugin.

commands.reason: 'Open today's daily note' is documented. Needs the Daily notes core plugin.
commands.does: Finds Open today's daily note. Needs the Daily notes core plugin.

commands.reason: 'Add file property' is documented as a command.
commands.does: Finds Add file property, for tags, dates and other note details.

commands.reason: 'Toggle checkbox status' does not appear in Obsidian's official help (checked the help source).

sections.name: Teams
sections.where: the Teams message box (any chat, channel or meeting chat) or the search bar at the top
sections.prereq: Teams desktop app only. Your organization can turn some commands off.
sections.blurb: Built into Microsoft Teams on desktop. Type / in a message box or in the search bar.
sections.note: Microsoft says built-in slash commands work only in Teams desktop. Most work in the message box; /chat works only in the search bar.

commands.reason: Listed for both message box and search bar.
commands.does: Sets your status to Available.

commands.reason: Listed for both.
commands.does: Sets your status to Busy.

commands.reason: Listed for both.
commands.does: Sets your status to Be right back.

commands.reason: Listed for both.
commands.does: Sets your status to Away.

commands.reason: Listed for both.
commands.does: Sets your status to Do not disturb.

commands.reason: Listed for both. Ctrl+G does the same thing.
commands.does: Jumps straight to a chat or channel.

commands.reason: Search bar only, per Microsoft's table. Label it that way.
commands.does: Sends a quick message from the search bar.

commands.reason: Message box only.
commands.does: Starts or joins a quick meeting.

commands.reason: Message box only.
commands.does: Schedules the message you're writing to send later.

commands.reason: Message box only; /unmute is also listed.
commands.does: Mutes the current chat. /unmute turns it back on.

commands.reason: Message box only.
commands.does: Inserts a code block in your message.

sections.name: GitHub Copilot
sections.where: the GitHub Copilot Chat box in your code editor
sections.prereq: GitHub Copilot extension signed in, in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains or Xcode. This is GitHub Copilot, not Microsoft Copilot.
sections.blurb: GitHub Copilot Chat in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs and Xcode. Each editor offers a different set.
sections.note: The list changes by editor and over time. Type / in Copilot Chat to see what yours offers.

commands.reason: Listed for VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains and Xcode.
commands.does: Explains how the selected code works.
commands.add: Select the code first. Add a question if you have one.
commands.example: /explain why this loop skips the last item
commands.platforms: VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Xcode

commands.reason: Listed for all four editors.
commands.does: Proposes a fix for problems in the selected code.
commands.add: Select the code. Paste the error if there is one.
commands.platforms: VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Xcode

commands.reason: Listed for all four editors.
commands.does: Writes unit tests for the selected code.
commands.add: Select the code. Name your test framework.
commands.platforms: VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Xcode

commands.reason: Listed for Visual Studio and Xcode only.
commands.does: Adds a documentation comment for the function or class.
commands.add: Put the cursor on the function or class.

commands.reason: Listed for Visual Studio only.
commands.does: Suggests ways to make the selected code run faster.

commands.reason: Listed for Xcode only.
commands.does: Simplifies the selected code.

commands.reason: In VS Code it creates a new project. On GitHub.com the same /new starts a new conversation instead. Not listed for other editors.
commands.does: Starts a new project from a description.
commands.example: /new a Flask app with one page and a contact form

commands.reason: Only listed for VS Code (starts a new chat session) and Copilot on GitHub.com (clears the conversation).
commands.does: Clears the chat so you can start fresh.

commands.reason: Listed for VS Code, Visual Studio and JetBrains, not Xcode.
commands.does: Shows a quick guide to using Copilot Chat.

search_key.name: Web
search_key.reason: YouTube, GitHub and Gmail confirmed in official help. MDN has no official page saying / focuses search, so drop it. Slash Guide is the owner's own site; confirm it on the live page.
search_key.does: Press / on many websites to jump straight to the search box, no mouse needed.
search_key.add: Just the / key, then type what you're looking for.
search_key.example: On YouTube, press / and type: how to repot a bonsai
works: Gmail (turn on keyboard shortcuts in Settings first)
search_key.blurb: Not a command you type into a box: a key that takes you to the box.

add_suggestions.does: Adds a GIF to your message.
Shows the messages and files you saved for later.
Turns the current block into a different type, like a heading or to-do.
add_suggestions.add: Pick the new block type from the list.
add_suggestions.where_override: at the start or end of a block

add_suggestions.does: Finds and fixes a failing test.
add_suggestions.add: Run your tests first so there's a failure to fix.
